doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Vocalists, novelty songs and the sing-along bomb
summary: Alumni All-Stars had Dottie Parker as vocalist, the Catatonic Five never sang; Sherman sings novelty songs of the Fallacious Five and recalls their own, including Semperubi Sabbubi.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah. Did you ever have vocalists in the group by choice?
Yes we did. We did. Mike Parker, the son of Paul Parker, was our first trumpeter. And he had wife named Dottie.
I know about that, yes.
And she was the vocalist.
Right. I think I was referring more to back in the Catatonic Five though. Did you have singing?
No.
Okay.
Never sang.
Okay. You know maybe that’s what to me distinguishes and is so neat about the fact that you guys did that, is nowadays popular music is so vocal oriented.
Yeah.
I mean you can listen all day to the radio, any station you want, and you hardly ever hear an instrumental.
Right. It’s rare.
So for you guys to have an instrumental band back then, I think it’s very hip.

Now this is odd that you say that, Monk, because our predecessors, the Fallacious Five, didn’t really have vocalists, but they used to, two or three of them, would intone lyrics to jazz type tunes like “She Looks Like Helen Brown.” I think you may know that one?
“She Looks Like Hell In Brown?”

Both. [sings] “She looks like Helen Brown/She’s the hottest gal in town/When she’s dressed in green or gray/Scotsmen throw their kilts away/Oh she looks like hell in brown/She’s the hottest gal in town/Oh she looks alright when she’s dressed in white/But she looks like hell in brown. That kind of thing.
Okay.
Novelty songs. Novelty songs like that. “Your Engine’s Kind of Rusty,” you know that one?
No.

Let me overhaul your car? [sings] Your engine’s kind of rusty/Cranky, kind of dusty/Let me overhaul your car/Your engine needs a workout/I’ll get every quirk out/My repairs are best by far/Say, why don’t you let me look under your hood/A pint of my oil will do your engine lots of good/And don’t you try and back out/I have got my jack out and we’re going to do it/Get out and get under/Oh let me overhaul your car. Always something suggestive.
That’s great.

Now in our band you just made me think, and we did have some songs that we sang, like “Sandy Don’t Allow no Jazz on Sunday,” and the “Coast Guard March,” this thing Semperubi Sabbubi. You’ve heard about that one?
No.

Oh wow. We decided to go Latin and kind of sophomoric but we discovered that the Latin phrase Semperubi Sabbubi can be translated “always wear underwear.” So to the tune of “Semper Paratus” we did it.
Okay.
But it wasn’t a great success so we dropped it from the act.
I see. And the Marine Corps didn’t really adopt it.
No, none of them fought to be recognized by our band. But in the 2004 predecessor of this particular CD the words are all printed out. We had attempted to have a sing-a-long but it was a bomb.
I think I was, Saturday night, I was there.
What a bomb ey? Woo hoo.
Yeah. Seemed like a good idea at the time but—
It was too sophomoric. They didn’t want to do that.
